originalText:
Alongside the Reno16 Series, OPPO also launched the new OPPO Bubble.

It is essentially a small display for remote camera preview/control that can be magnetically attached to the rear side of your phone.

It is useful to see your pose and composition when your phone is placed elsewhere or when someone else is taking the photo for you.

Here’s what you can do with it:
✅ Shutter button
✅ Zoom control (with pre-determined zoom levels: 0.6x, 1x, 2x, and 3.5x, it depends on the phone model)
✅ Switch between the photo and video modes
✅ Rear camera mirror and timer/countdown
✅ Switch the preview modes from full-view and fit-to-width
✅ Adjust the brightness of the badge with 3 different levels (up to 600 nits brightness)

OPPO Bubble works effectively as a remote camera control from up to 10 metres away.

During my testing period, I really love using the OPPO Bubble as I think it is truly helpful when taking a group photo or direct my friends/family to frame the photo.

The display looks gorgeous too, as it is a 1.73” OLED panel that is bright and vibrant.

That means your wallpapers will also look stunning here, as if you’re viewing it on the phone’s screen.

Unlike other similar solutions, OPPO Bubble is very thin and lightweight, at only 7 mm thick & 27.5 grams in weight. It is also IP54-certified for dust and splash resistance.

The battery capacity itself is at 560 mAh, rated to last for up to 49.7 hours when displaying a static image or 7.8 hours when continuously displaying the camera preview.

But, I found several things that I need OPPO to fix via a software update (or for the next-gen product):
• The functions are limited to camera control and adjusting a few system settings (brightness, screen lock, and scheduled screen off).
• It would’ve been so much better if the camera app functionality is expanded, for example: LED flash control, switching to more modes, EV control, filter picking, and more.
• It would’ve been awesome if they can expand the functionality, for example: music control, stopwatch/timer, notification peeking, and more.
• The magnet on the rear side of the Bubble is not as strong as I expected, so when placed on a magnetic case, it can easily move around or rotate, which makes it a bit harder to use.
• It is supposed to work with the Reno16 Series, but none of those phones have an included magnetic case or a magnetic back cover. You have to add the magnets on your own to attach it to the back side of your phone.
• Even though the circular shape might be visually appealing, it makes the viewfinder narrower and more limited.
• I found some software issues that happened quite rarely, like how it would fail to change the wallpaper, the connection suddenly dropping, and the camera app opening slowly.

OPPO Bubble is currently supported by 13 OPPO phones (Find X8/X9 Series, Reno16 Series, Reno14/15 Series except the F models), and compatibility with other devices will be coming soon.

Also, OPPO will extend support for OPPO Bubble to iPhone X and later models, running iOS 15 or later.

The full rollout is expected to be completed by July 7 in the worldwide market.

I think the potential of this device is extremely high. With a few tweaks, refinements, and better readiness, I can assure you that it will be a successful product.

originalText:
Google just shipped AI Edge Eloquent — a free dictation app that removes filler words in real time, runs entirely offline, and it's already on iOS.

No internet needed. Your voice data never leaves the device.

Here's why this matters more than another transcription tool:

Most dictation apps transcribe everything — every "um", "uh", mid-sentence correction, restart. You get raw speech as text, which still needs editing. AI Edge Eloquent flips this: it captures what you MEANT to say, not what you actually said.

The offline engine uses Google's Gemma architecture on-device. Enable online mode and it taps Gemini for deeper cleanup, smart rewrites, and key-point extraction.

You can import your Gmail contacts and jargon via Dictionaries tab — names, niche terms, industry acronyms. Accuracy improves over time as it learns your vocabulary.

Output options:
- Polish → clean, readable text
- Key Points → summary (online only)
- Formal / Short / Long rewrites

Plus WPM stats and word count — useful for anyone tracking speaking clarity.

Why I'm watching this: Google is quietly building the on-device AI stack. Gemma → AI Edge → now Eloquent. The same pattern as Pixel's on-device AI features — but this time it's a standalone iOS app, not tied to any hardware.

If it comes to Android, it replaces Wispr Flow, MacWhisper, and SuperWhisper for anyone who values privacy over cloud features.

Free, no account required, works offline. That's a rare combination.

originalText:
The most underrated desk upgrade of the year is free. It uses the iPad you already own.

A guy on GitHub released OpenSidecar. Free. Open source. peetzweg/opensidecar. You install it on a Mac and any spare Apple device becomes a full second monitor. An old iPad. An iPhone. A second MacBook.

Not a mirror. A real extension of your desktop. You drag a browser window from the Mac straight onto the iPad, scroll with your finger, move around the page like the tablet is a monitor you can hold.

Until this week, that feature cost $100. Duet Display. Luna Display. Apple's own Sidecar with a locked list of supported devices. Three paid products doing what one open source repo now does over Wi-Fi or USB with macOS 14 and iOS 17.

The real idea in the post is not the app.

The real idea is that half the people watching have an iPad in a drawer that became a YouTube player, then a coaster, then dust. It has an M1 chip and a retina display and it is sitting three feet from a laptop that would kill for the extra screen.

Do not buy a second monitor. You already have one. You forgot about it.

The demo is a live prototype. Latency under video editing and games has not been tested. But for a browser window, a Notion doc, a Slack, a spreadsheet, it just works.

The best desk upgrade of the year is not a new display. It is the device you already stopped using.
